overall: The AG found the Conservation Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve minutes of 17 meetings held September 2022 to June 2023, but found the violation was not intentional; ordered compliance and approval of 13 remaining minutes within 40 days.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to timely approve minutes of its meetings held between September 2022 and June 2023.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Commission failed to timely approve all 17 sets of minutes of meetings, which were held between September 13, 2022, and June 27, 2023, where the minutes were not approved within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days following each meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the untimely minutes approval was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law; the AG considered whether it was intentional.
allegations.key_passage: Because we have not advised the Commission of its obligations prior to the events addressed in this letter, we find that this violation was not intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
Approve the 13 sets of minutes of meetings held between September 13, 2022, and March 28, 2023, within the next 40 days and certify to the AG's office that it has done so.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. In addition, we order the Commission to approve the 13 sets of minutes of meetings held between September 13, 2022, and March 28, 2023, within the next 40 days and to thereafter certify to our office that it has done so.
